findings.title: Hand-made escalation packs can overwrite the first review
quotes: run it twice more as independent jurors on copies of its pack whose
findings.fix: have the step write the `-2` and `-3` packs, or have it refuse a lens output file that a juror has overwritten after collect. Otherwise name the exact output paths in the skill and check them.

sources.situation: the orchestrator copies the blocker's fix-check pack for the `-2` and `-3` jurors and forgets to change `## Your output`, or changes only one copy. The juror writes `implementation-E-5-<lens>.md` again. The first review's findings are replaced by a fix-check output that has no findings. Collect sees a valid file, so the confirmed blocker disappears with no error, or the three votes count the same file three times.

findings.reason: SKILL.md lines 73-77 have the orchestrator hand-copy the blocker's fix-check pack and edit `## Your output`, and the text says "the step never writes these". Nothing in the artefact makes collect or the step detect a juror that wrote the first-review filename, so the one-mistake overwrite is possible as written.

findings.title: The 15-call test counts calls by hand and may miss the `--run` call
quotes: Now 15: plan (1), pack (1), step (1), 4 jurors (4), step (1), refuter (1), step (1), one dispose (1),
findings.fix: count real calls by the next: lines the test follows, or state in the skill whether the `--run` call is needed for spec gates. Make the test follow the `next:` lines.

sources.situation: the skill requires `nio jury next` and then `nio jury next --run <run>`, but the test calls the step once before the juror outputs exist. If the second call is required, scenario A takes 16 calls and AC-11 fails, yet the test still passes. If the second call is not required, the skill sends the orchestrator to an unneeded call. Because `calls` is a manual tally, no change to the skill can make the test fail.

findings.title: The skill-wording test skips the blocks most likely to keep old calls
quotes: kept = [b for b in steps.split("\n\n") if "--blocker" not in b and "--human" not in b]
findings.fix: exempt only the single allowed command strings, not whole blocks.

sources.situation: the escalation and human-disposal text is exempt from the check for `nio jury collect`, `nio jury check` and the other dropped calls. A leftover separate call there passes, and CT-6 asks for all of them to go.

findings.title: The AC-11 call count is a hand-kept counter, not a measurement
findings.fix: accept it, since the step is the only call path the test exercises and `test_nfr1_skill_names_the_step` guards the skill text. Optionally derive the count from the calls the test makes.

sources.situation: the test adds to `calls` by hand after each step it performs. If the skill later asked for an extra call, such as a separate collect, the counter would still read 15 and the test would pass.

findings.title: Plan-gate section still tells the orchestrator to read status with `nio jury check`
quotes: The plan jury is then paused (`nio jury check <slug> plan` prints
findings.fix: name the step for this state too, e.g. "`nio jury next <slug> plan` prints `state: waiting-on-spec`".

sources.situation: the diff rewrites the same plan-gate section to say "While the step prints `state: with-human`, it refuses a new round", so the skill now reads status from the step. The sentence a few lines earlier still sends the orchestrator to `nio jury check <slug> plan` to see `state: waiting-on-spec`, a call CT-6 says the skill drops. An orchestrator following the skill runs the removed command for one state and the step for another.

findings.reason: implementation-E-5-consistency: the skill text now says `nio jury next <slug> plan` prints `state: waiting-on-spec` (`skills/jury/SKILL.md`, the plan-gate paragraph). The CLI does not do that. `plan()` (`src/nio/jury.py:258`) prints no state line, and `next` only raises the paused message when new packs arrive (`jury.py:608-609`). The `state:` line comes from `nio jury check <slug> plan` (`jury.py:1121`). The fix ask's example is what the code does not do, so the sentence needs to name `nio jury check <slug> plan`, or the CLI must print the line from `next`.
findings.where: skills/jury/SKILL.md, "At the plan gate", "Findings rooted in the spec"

findings.title: The skill's intro still names `nio check spec <slug> --gate` as a call to run
quotes: Takes a spec that passes `nio check spec <slug> --gate` to a verdict
findings.fix: reword the intro to "Takes a spec the step can check (`nio jury next` checks the gate)", or keep the precondition and say the step repeats it.

sources.situation: CT-6 says the step "checks the gate itself" and the skill drops its `nio check <gate> --gate` calls. The intro still reads as a precondition the orchestrator must run before the jury. A host that follows it runs a gate check the step already does, which is the extra call FR-11 removes. If the gate check is kept as a precondition the human sees, say so in the intro, so the two readings do not conflict.

findings.title: CT-6 says the skill drops `nio jury check`, but the human-override line keeps it
findings.fix: add to CT-6 "except `nio jury check <slug> <gate> --record --human`, which C-261028-quyk keeps", or move the human-closed route to the step if the step can take `--human`.

sources.situation: the "Other outcomes" text keeps `nio jury check <slug> spec --record --human "<their reason>"` for the human-closed gate. The test `test_nfr1_skill_names_the_step` skips any block that contains `--human`, so the skill passes, but CT-6 as written does not allow this call. The memory record C-261028-quyk (change accepted: "--human at a jury gate goes through nio jury check") requires this route, so the skill is probably right and CT-6's list of dropped calls is too broad. Either the spec or the CT-6 wording needs to say that `--record --human` stays.

findings.title: AC-11 test counts its own increments, so it cannot fail
findings.fix: Derive the count from real events, such as the `next:` lines the step printed plus the pack and output files. Or drop the "at most 15" claim from the test and leave AC-11 to its human check.

findings.title: The skill test skips the whole step-2 block, so the removed calls could come back unnoticed
quotes: kept = [b for b in steps.split("\n\n") if "--blocker" not in b and "--human" not in b]
findings.fix: Remove only the exempt line from the text, not the whole paragraph. Or allow just `nio jury fixcheck ... --blocker` and check everything else.

sources.situation: In SKILL.md, step 2 is one paragraph with no blank lines, and its escalate bullet contains `--blocker`. The filter therefore drops that whole paragraph before the banned-call check. A later edit that put `nio jury collect` or `nio agents sync` back into step 2 would pass the test. The skill's mention of `nio jury fixcheck` is only exempt because of that same filter.

findings.title: Stale `nio jury check` and record wording remains in the skill
quotes: The plan jury is then paused (`nio jury check <slug> plan` prints
findings.fix: Say "the step prints `state: waiting-on-spec`" and "call the step again". Keep `nio jury check --record --human` only for the human's close, and say that is its one use.

sources.situation: CT-6 says the skill drops its `nio jury check` calls, and the plan-gate "With the human" bullet was updated to say "the step prints". The change-request bullet in the same section still tells the orchestrator to read `state: waiting-on-spec` from `nio jury check`. "When to stop" still says every ruling is recorded by `--record`, and the implementation bullet says to wait "before you check again". An orchestrator may therefore make a separate check call beside the step, which the skill is meant to prevent.

findings.where: skills/jury/SKILL.md (plan gate section, "When to stop", and the implementation "waiting on a change request" bullet)
